title: Unnamed Road, 5291 Miren, Slovenia - Pine forest in the wind
author: Bojan Marusic
notes: Pine forest in steady wind, Miren (Slovenia), MixPre-II + LOM Usi Pro (pro gear; only a 320 kbps MP3 is published). Airy needle hiss 300 Hz-5 kHz with gentle-to-moderate gusts every 20-40 s and calm lulls; no birds, voices, traffic or bumps seen. Sub-100 Hz content is acoustic forest roar (L/R coherent +0.95, not mic buffeting); optional HPF ~60 Hz. Region-neutral (no fauna).

title: Unnamed Road, 5291 Miren, Slovenia - Pine forest in the wind
author: Bojan Marusic
notes: Second, non-overlapping 240 s section of the same Miren pine-wind take (different gust sequence) so the two wind beds can be crossfaded without audible repetition. Same character/caveats as wind-1 (skip first 10 s fade-in).

title: Nanos 10a, 5271 Vipava, Slovenia - Wind in pine forest
author: Bojan Marusic
notes: Bora gale (gusts to 85 km/h, -8 C) through a pine forest, Vipava (Slovenia), LOM Usi Pro + MixPre-3 II, 320 kbps MP3. Dense, bright roaring hiss with continuous surging gusts - the heavier storm layer. No precipitation audible (it is a cold dry gale, not literally falling snow). Strong but L/R-coherent energy below 80 Hz (acoustic, not buffeting): HPF ~70-80 Hz recommended.

title: Trnovo, Slovenia - Wind in Trnovo forest
author: Bojan Marusic
notes: Strong north wind at 3 a.m. in Trnovo forest (Slovenia), February; LOM Usi Pro in BBG windjammer, MixPre-3 II, 320 kbps MP3. Darker, distant canopy roar (energy 60 Hz-3 kHz), the most intense section of a 22-min take; extremely even, no events, no birds (night). Alternative heavy-weather layer; can also sit under wind-1/2 at low level.

title: Spadelsberg, 72639 Neuffen, Deutschland - fireplace
author: Hoerma
notes: Fire crackling ('Knistern'), Spadelsberg/Neuffen (Germany), 48 kHz/24-bit FLAC. Dense fine crackles (approx. 1 per second, 1.5-14 kHz) over a soft flame roar; first 55 s (stronger roar/flare-up) excluded. Source page only says 'fireplace' - could be an open hearth rather than a closed stove. LF roar is coherent (acoustic).

title: Colonel's House (fireplace), Kłodzko, Poland - 944 fireplace hiss and crackling
author: Piotrek Zyla
notes: Indoor fireplace hiss and crackling, Colonel's House, Klodzko (Poland); Sennheiser MKH 8020 AB pair on Zoom F3, 96 kHz/24-bit. Very clean, steady, roar-dominated (60-250 Hz) with sparse crackles. Only 84 s long (shorter than the 90 s target) - use as a second fire texture / crossfade partner for fire-1.

title: Petersburg Borough, Alaska, United States - Snow Crunching on Frozen Lake
author: isaiahbowenkarlyn (Isaiah Bowen-Karlyn)
notes: About 8 footsteps crunching in ~3 in of snow over a frozen reservoir (-7 C), Petersburg Borough, Alaska; Zoom H4n FLAC. Continuous walk cut at inter-step gaps (needs short fades). Recordist's own steps = close perspective; mono downmix safe (L/R +0.21, <3 dB loss).

title: Petersburg Borough, Alaska, United States - Snow Crunching on Frozen Lake
author: isaiahbowenkarlyn (Isaiah Bowen-Karlyn)
notes: Same Alaska walk, a different stretch of ~9 steps that ends in a natural pause (walker stops), giving a different rhythm/ending from snowsteps-1.

title: Walk in Snow
author: Moodist (remvze); original uploader via Pixabay/CC0 (not credited in repo)
notes: Close, slow footsteps in cold, squeaky snow (~9 steps, tonal 300 Hz-1.5 kHz 'squeak' typical of very cold snow). 48 kHz MP3 from Moodist with ~16.5 kHz lossy ceiling. Different texture from the Alaska crunch.

title: Utena, Lithuania, snow falls from trees
author: alas23/sala
notes: Snow sifting/falling from snow-laden branches after a night of heavy snow, Utena (Lithuania). Soft broadband 'shhh' of granules (2-14 kHz) about 23 dB over a very quiet floor. Not a heavy 'whump' - a light slump/sift. Quiet file (-46 LUFS): needs gain; faint 300-1000 Hz background drone (distant).

title: Utena, Lithuania, snow falls from trees
author: alas23/sala
notes: Second snow sift/slump from the same Utena snowy-tree recording (~22 dB over floor). Same caveats as snowfall-1.

title: Utena, Lithuania, snow falls from trees
author: alas23/sala
notes: Third, softer and longer snow-sift event (~16 dB over floor) from the Utena snowy trees. Low SNR - use at low level / distance.

title: Utena, Lithuania, moaning tree in winters wind
author: alas23/sala
notes: Two pine trunks rubbing in winter wind - rhythmic stick-slip creak with ~800 Hz tonal 'moan' + harmonics, ~30 dB over floor. Contact mics (inside-the-wood perspective, bandwidth ~4 kHz, heavy sub-200 Hz thump): HPF ~200 Hz recommended; mono sum safe.

title: Utena, Lithuania, moaning tree in winters wind
author: alas23/sala
notes: Longer creak series (~10 pulses) from the same two rubbing pines, Utena winter wind; same contact-mic caveats (HPF ~200 Hz).

title: Utena, Lithuania, winterscape
author: alas23/sala
notes: Frost crack in snow-loaded trees at -8 C, Utena (Lithuania), air mics (binaural-processed): sharp broadband crack (+38 dB over a very quiet floor) followed by a smaller second crack, natural short tail. Mono downmix safe for this segment (L/R +0.63).

title: Utena, Lithuania, winterscape
author: alas23/sala
notes: Single loud frost crack from the same -8 C Utena snowy-forest recording (+38 dB over floor), clean pre/post silence.

title: Chuncheon Lake Ice Formation , Gangwon-do, South Korea - Chuncheon Lake Ice Formation
author: abyssence
notes: Frozen-lake ice 'singing': small precursor tick then a loud crack with the classic dispersive downward 'pew' sweep (~1 kHz to 200 Hz) ringing across the basin. Chuncheon Lake (Korea) during rapid freeze-up, FLAC. Background: steady low rumble below ~800 Hz at about -45 dBFS (events +20-30 dB).

title: Chuncheon Lake Ice Formation , Gangwon-do, South Korea - Chuncheon Lake Ice Formation
author: abyssence
notes: Single lake-ice ping/pew with short descending tail (Chuncheon Lake freeze-up), ~22 dB over floor.

title: Chuncheon Lake Ice Formation , Gangwon-do, South Korea - Chuncheon Lake Ice Formation
author: abyssence
notes: Single sharp lake-ice crack-ping with dispersive tail (+27 dB), Chuncheon Lake.

title: Chuncheon Lake Ice Formation , Gangwon-do, South Korea - Chuncheon Lake Ice Formation
author: abyssence
notes: Two lake-ice events ~1 s apart (tick, then a pew with a longer descending tail), Chuncheon Lake.

title: Chuncheon Lake Ice Formation , Gangwon-do, South Korea - Chuncheon Lake Ice Formation
author: abyssence
notes: Lake-ice pew with a low thump component (heaving sheet), Chuncheon Lake, ~19 dB over floor.

title: Sound Gallery - Red-breasted Nuthatch (Yosemite National Park)
author: U.S. National Park Service (Natural Sounds & Night Skies)
notes: Red-breasted Nuthatch nasal 'yank' calls (6 notes), Yosemite NP. Very quiet clip (-47 LUFS, needs ~+30 dB gain) and band-limited to ~4.5 kHz by NPS processing; clean otherwise. Western/boreal conifer species, fits the region set.

title: Sound Gallery - Clark's Nutcracker (Yosemite National Park)
author: U.S. National Park Service (Natural Sounds & Night Skies)
notes: Clark's Nutcracker: three loud grating 'kraaa' calls, Yosemite NP; close, clean, MP3 128k (~15 kHz ceiling). Corvid of high western conifer forests, often heard in snowy winter woods.

title: Sound Gallery - Common Raven (Grand Teton National Park)
author: U.S. National Park Service (Natural Sounds & Night Skies)
notes: Common Raven: two deep 'kraak' croaks, Grand Teton NP (Wyoming). Croaks are clean (1-3 kHz harmonics) but sit on strong sub-150 Hz wind rumble: HPF ~300 Hz required.

title: Sound Gallery - Common Raven (Grand Teton National Park)
author: U.S. National Park Service (Natural Sounds & Night Skies)
notes: Common Raven, second pair of croaks from the same Grand Teton clip (different inflection). Same HPF ~300 Hz caveat.

title: HAMBIO #3862: Great Horned Owl @ Short Hills Nature Sanctuary, 2019-03-01 12:52:15.840
author: Hamilton Naturalists' Club (Hamilton Bioacoustics Research Project)
notes: Great Horned Owl territorial hoot series 'hoo h'hoo-hoo hooo hoo' (~250-300 Hz), Short Hills Nature Sanctuary, Ontario, March 1; autonomous recorder 48 kHz FLAC, ~23-25 dB over band floor at a natural distance. Light low rumble below ~180 Hz: HPF ~150 Hz. Attribution: Hamilton Naturalists' Club, CC BY 4.0.
